claims.claim: Hong Kong should tighten rent control on subdivided units through tenure security and an indexed initial-rent band, not a hard cap on initial rents.
The binding constraint on SDU households is the length of the public-housing queue and the insecurity of tenancy, not the price of a cubicle.
The long-run elasticity of SDU-type supply is 0.31 to 0.48, so a 10 percent cap-induced rent cut removes roughly 3 to 5 percent of stock over five years.
First-generation rent controls (hard caps on levels) show consistent contraction, while second-generation controls (caps on increases within tenancies) show small or null effects.
Hong Kong's 2021 Tenancy Control Ordinance is second-generation, capping increases within a tenancy but leaving the initial rent untouched.
The SDU stock grew from 100,800 units in 2019 to 111,200 in 2025 despite the Tenancy Control Ordinance.
SDU tenants pay a 15 to 25 percent per-square-foot premium over mainstream flats.
Real rent burden worsened from 31 to 34 percent of income even under the ordinance.
A hard cap would free about 800 dollars a month for incumbents like Mr Chan, equivalent to a month of food.
A tightened-cap scenario yields a net transfer of roughly 900 dollars per month to incumbents, while 3,000 to 4,000 households per year are unable to enter the segment.
In Berlin, capped initial-offer rents fell sharply, listing supply contracted within a year, and when the law was struck down suppressed increases released above the pre-cap trend line.
New York's stabilisation scheme shows modest contraction because it is light at first-rent.
Current inspection capacity covers under 6 percent of stock per year, and a band-based initial-rent cap would require a certifiable tenancy register costing 40 to 60 staff-years.
The subcommittee could not identify any enforcement design under which the newest-arrival tail is protected first rather than last.
An NGO survey of 440 households found 61 percent would trade a nominal rent increase for three-year security of tenure, and 74 percent for a faster public-housing offer.
An indexed, reviewable per-square-foot band sits on firmer legal ground than a hard cap, which would attract compensation claims and judicial review.
Policy should enforce fire, partition and ventilation standards; mandate written tenancy agreements and minimum notice periods; and publish an initial-rent band that binds without confiscating.
A hard cap would help incumbents while handing the bill to the next family outside the door, in a city where the public-housing queue runs five and a half years.

cites.sentence: Standard theory predicts contraction under binding ceilings, but the magnitude is an empirical question, and the reviewed literature puts the long-run elasticity of SDU-type supply at 0.31 to 0.48: a 10 percent cap-induced rent cut removes roughly 3 to 5 percent of stock over five years [D6p1].

Crucially, the paper distinguishes first-generation controls (hard caps on levels), which show consistent contraction, from second-generation controls (caps on increases within tenancies), which show small or null effects [D6p2].
Hong Kong's 2021 Tenancy Control Ordinance is second-generation — it capped increases within a tenancy but left the initial rent untouched [D1p3]
— and the stock grew from 100,800 units in 2019 to 111,200 in 2025 straight through it [D2p1].

On a per-square-foot basis SDU tenants already pay a 15 to 25 percent premium over mainstream flats [D1p1], and real rent burden worsened from 31 to 34 percent of income even under the ordinance [D2p2].

On a per-square-foot basis SDU tenants already pay a 15 to 25 percent premium over mainstream flats [D1p1], and real rent burden worsened from 31 to 34 percent of income even under the ordinance [D2p2].
Mrs Wong, nine years in an SDU with no written agreement, reports the ordinance changed nothing she can see: the landlord still charges whatever the market of desperate newcomers bears [D4p1].
A hard cap would address exactly this pain — Mr Chan estimates it would free about 800 dollars a month, a month of food [D3p2].

The modelled tightened-cap scenario yields a net transfer of roughly 900 dollars per month to incumbents, against 3,000 to 4,000 households per year unable to enter the segment, mostly new arrivals and newly formed households [D6p4].

Berlin is the cautionary case: capped initial-offer rents fell sharply, listing supply contracted within a year as owners withheld or rerouted flats, and when the law was struck down the suppressed increases released above the pre-cap trend line [D7p1][D7p2].

Berlin is the cautionary case: capped initial-offer rents fell sharply, listing supply contracted within a year as owners withheld or rerouted flats, and when the law was struck down the suppressed increases released above the pre-cap trend line [D7p1][D7p2].
New York's stabilisation scheme, by contrast, shows modest contraction precisely because it is light at first-rent [D8p2]
Current inspection capacity covers under 6 percent of stock per year, and a band-based initial-rent cap would require a certifiable tenancy register costing 40 to 60 staff-years to stand up [D10p1].
More damning, the subcommittee could not identify any enforcement design under which the newest-arrival tail — the population the policy names — is protected first rather than last [D10p3].
The tenants least able to complain are those with no written agreement, like Mrs Wong [D4p1], so enforcement would systematically miss the most exploited.
The NGO survey of 440 households found 61 percent would trade a nominal rent increase for three-year security of tenure, and 74 percent for a faster public-housing offer [D11p1].
Mr Chan, asked what would help most, does not name rent; he names the waiting list [D3p3].

Counsel advises that an indexed, reviewable per-square-foot band — rate-capping rather than confiscation — sits on firmer legal ground than a hard cap, which would attract compensation claims and judicial review [D9p1][D9p2].

Counsel advises that an indexed, reviewable per-square-foot band — rate-capping rather than confiscation — sits on firmer legal ground than a hard cap, which would attract compensation claims and judicial review [D9p1][D9p2].
The Chief Executive's expected "floor-standard + rent band" package points the same way [D12p1].

A hard cap would help incumbents like Mr Chan's 800 dollars while handing the bill to the next family still outside the door — and in a city where the queue runs five and a half years [D1p2], that is not a trade worth making.
